guarantees.claim: cmd_update is driven as a direct wire copy of reg2hw.cmd.cmd.qe.
cmd_q is assigned the cast kmac_cmd_e'(reg2hw.cmd.cmd.q).
sw_cmd is cmd_q when cmd_update is true, otherwise CmdNone.

assumptions.claim: reg2hw.cmd.cmd.qe produces a glitch-free one-cycle pulse per SW command write, synchronous to local clock.
assumptions.risk: If qe toggles multiple times or is asynchronous, cmd_update may cause duplicated or missed commands downstream.

assumptions.claim: reg2hw.cmd.cmd.q must be a legal kmac_cmd_e encoding when reg2hw.cmd.cmd.qe is active.
assumptions.risk: An illegal raw command value would be forwarded as an invalid enum, leading to undefined behavior in downstream command decode.

assumptions.claim: Downstream consumers must capture sw_cmd (or cmd_q) on the cycle when cmd_update is high; after cmd_update deasserts, sw_cmd returns to CmdNone.
assumptions.risk: If a downstream sink samples sw_cmd later or expects it to persist, it may lose the command and interpret CmdNone as idle, potentially stalling or missing operations.

uncertain_points.claim: An illegal command value written to reg2hw.cmd.cmd.q is directly forwarded to sw_cmd without error checking when cmd_update is high.
uncertain_points.cond: when cmd_update=1 and raw q is not a valid kmac_cmd_e
uncertain_points.risk: Downstream command decoding may misinterpret the illegal value, potentially entering insecure or unexpected states (e.g., inadvertently triggering secret processing or bypassing abort).

uncertain_points.claim: The generate condition determining the `gen_no_cmd_delay_buf` path (else branch) is not visible; this chunk assumes direct combinational forwarding is safe.
uncertain_points.risk: If the condition is inadvertently true while a delay buffer is needed, the combinational path may violate timing between the SW write and downstream use of cmd_update/cmd_q, potentially causing hold-time violations or missed commands.
